title: Catalog pages show older prices
briefing: A support escalation reports old prices on a subset of catalog pages. Use edge and origin records to narrow the issue.

actions.label: Compare the catalog origin response
actions.criteria: Use when it is unclear whether old content comes from origin or the cache.
actions.instructions: Compare the origin revision with the affected edge response for the same product and locale.

actions.label: Inspect the purge key mapping
actions.criteria: Use when the purge addresses a different cache key than the affected request.
actions.instructions: Compare the request cache key fields with the cache purge selector.

actions.label: Inspect regional edge health
actions.criteria: Use when a region-specific outage or increased edge failures could account for the symptom.
actions.instructions: Compare request volume, latency, and errors for the affected and healthy edge regions.

fallback: Collect an affected product URL, its locale, and the corresponding edge response headers.

events.text: Two customers report different prices for SKU 882. Tickets omit the source response, location, and cache status.
Affected catalog response: locale fr-CA, edge=HIT, revision=r71. The current expected revision is r72. The origin response for fr-CA was not sampled.
Catalog requests build the edge cache selector from the exact requested locale. The legacy locale group key is retained only for admin previews.
Purge completed successfully for SKU 882 and selector fr.

debrief.summary: The purge targeted fr while the affected edge request keyed its response under fr-CA. The origin already held the latest price.
lessons: A successful purge can target the wrong key.
Pair the purge selector with the cache key definition and affected response.
